text:
maya: FYI — DLQ replay this morning left a bunch of orphaned traces. When messages were requeued the worker started fresh spans instead of joining original trace. Anyone have a simple pattern for dead-letter -> replay trace resurrection?
serge: We hit this before. Main problem: broker strips headers or we regenerate message-id so traceparent is gone.
eli: Do we even try to preserve full W3C traceparent through DLQs? SQS drops arbitrary custom headers on some flows.
jun: We currently attach x-rw-trace (base64 signed blob) as message attribute for SQS and kafka headers for kafka. DLQs keep attributes for kafka but SQS dead-letter wiring sometimes loses them depending on consumer lib.
maya: TL;DR: some messages keep a small token, others lose everything. Replays that re-publish create new trace ids. We want to stitch back to original trace if token still exists.
serge: Proposal: canonicalize a tiny span carrier: {trace_id, parent_id, sampled_flags, sig, ts} encoded as compact base64. Keep size < 128 bytes so brokers like nsq/sqs/kafka OK. Verify signature on replay and attach as baggage to rehydrated span.
eli: Sounds reasonable. Two questions: 1) TTL on that token? 2) What about sampling decision consistency — if original was not sampled can we create a span on replay for debugging?
jun: TTL = 7 days? Need to balance retention and token validity for long retries. For sampling, we should honor original sampled flag. If sampled=0 we only create meta-span with sampling=false tag so we can link without storing payloads.
serge: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
def extract_or_reconstruct(msg):
    tok = msg.attrs.get('x-rw-trace') or msg.headers.get('trace-token')
    if not tok: return None
    payload = b64decode(tok)
    if not verify_sig(payload): return None
    if payload.ts < now() - TTL: return None
    return {trace_id: payload.tid, parent_id: payload.pid, flags: payload.f}
```
maya: Nice. Also need to handle replay-through-deadletter where original worker emitted exporter spans to OTLP already. We should avoid duplicate span ids if replay produces same operations.
eli: Right — consumer should attach a new "message.replay" span with attribute linking to original trace_id (link semantic in OTEL) instead of trying to recreate exact span_id. That avoids collisions in the trace store and still gives visibility.
jun: So flow: on replay, if token verifies, create a small local span "message.replay" and add link to original trace_id/parent_id. If sampled=1 we also forward an event with original trace hints to the exporter.
telemetry-bot: Note: exporter quota implications — replay causing full span export will increase billed token counts. Consider sample rate cap for replay flows.
serge: Agreed. Add policy: replays sampled=1 exported only if org has replay-exports enabled or within replay budget. Otherwise mark with link-only and increment replay-metrics.
maya: Edge cases: what about messages that lost token entirely but have log traces correlating via timestamp + message-key? Can we heuristically stitch?
eli: Heuristics are brittle. Better to rely on a deterministic rekeying step at enqueue time: ensure every message gets an immutable trace-token persisted in an idempotent storage (redis) that survives DLQ flows. But that's extra infra.
jun: For now, prioritize compact signed token in attributes + replay link span. We'll draft a short RFC and a prototype in the gateway: extract/verify/attach link span.
maya: I'll draft RFC. Needs to cover header formats for SQS vs Kafka, signing key rotation, TTL, sampling policy, and telemetry budget opt-in.
serge: Also add test-cases: DLQ->requeue with header present, DLQ->requeue with header missing, DLQ replay after TTL expiry.
ops-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026. Assigned to maya. :spiral_note_pad:
maya: Thanks — will post RFC early tomorrow and ping for review. :thumbsup:
